Output 1: Forests, wetlands, and critical ecosystems are restored and conserved for nature-based solutions. Indicators
Indicator 1.1: Natural resources that are managed under a sustainable use, conservation, access and benefit-sharing regime (SP 1.4.1) Target: (a) Area of land under protection (3,916,486 Ha) (b) Area of existing protected area under improved management (4,000 Ha) (c) Area under sustainable forest management (800 Ha) d) Area of land under sustainable land management regime (2,800 Ha).
Result: The area is yet to be computed. Under the UNDP Anti-corruption for peace and inclusive societies (ACPIS) global project, a Natural Resource Information System (NARIS) has been set up for National Forestry Authority (NFA) and National Environmental Management Authority (NEMA) to enable monitoring of forest degradation and afforestation with intention to add more components to enhance monitoring of other environmental resources. Equipment including drones, data collections tablets, GIS workstation computers, large visualization screens, binoculars, GPS and laptops have been procured for both NFA and NEMA to support monitoring of forest and other natural resources and enhance operationalization of the NARIS platform.
Indicator 1.2 # of local governments and communities with robust/functional natural resource governance structures. Target:TBD Result: No achievement
Indicator 1.3 # of Platforms for knowledge/information sharing. Target:Two (2) Result: There are two (2) knowledge sharing platforms 1. Knowledge sharing platform on waste to energy 2. Knowledge sharing platform on use of Neem tree seeds as pesticides
Indicator 1.4: # non-state actors (CSOs, private sector, religious and cultural institutions) whose capacity is strengthened for advocating and implementing NbS. Target: TBD Result: Two (2) non-state actors were strengthened. UNDP Developed training manuals and trained 23 (13 male 10 females) UNDP&FAO staff and 36 (19 male, 17 female) partners on gender, environment, climate, and energy nexus; trained 12 (5 male, 7 female) UNDP&FAO staff and 42 partners (28 male, 14 female) on Social and Environmental Safeguards (SES) and also trained 36 (27 male 9 female) NEMA enforcement team member on ecosystems management.
Indicator 1.5.: # of communities with access to financing support for ecosystem restoration, protection and sustainable management of natural resources (e.g., PES/benefit sharing schemes, revolving fund schemes, cash for work, debt swap etc). Target: TBD Result: 11: 1. The wetland restoration project in Eastern Uganda conducted an assessment on PES and plans are underway to implement it in 5 districts (Kaliro, Namutumba, Butaleja, Budaka and Kibuku). 2. There are12 Revolving fund schemes established for 12 cooperatives in 6 Districts of Eastern Uganda (Bugiri, Budaka, Busia, Buyende, Kamuli, Kaliro , Namutumba) 3. A Cash for work scheme was established in the FSURE project for land preparation among the grantees supported by Hunger Fighters Uganda.
Indicator 1.6: Amount of financial resources mobilized and utilized for climate action (modified SP 2.5.1) Target: USD 600,000 Result: USD 540,000 was mobilized for Climate Promise Initiative.
Indicator 1.7: # of designated protected areas for the conservation of biodiversity. Target: TBD Result: There are 4 national parks and 3 forests namely; Queen Elizabeth national park, Mt Elgon national park, Bwindi Mugahinga Gorilla eco system, and Murkson and Karuma conservation area, Mabira forest, Karinzu Maramagambo forest and Sango bay forest. These are supported to reduce pressure on the protected area eco systems.
Indicator 1.8: # of diagnostic (knowledge products) on NbS best practices and lessons learned to influence/inform policy and practice. Target: TBD. Result: There are 2 knowledge products. 1. A policy brief on gender dimensions in environment, climate change and energy nexus in Uganda was developed. 2. The SCALA project in collaboration with the climate promise and NDC project developed the integrated Monitoring Reporting and Verification (iMRV) tool that will enhance reporting on the NDC targets for Uganda.
Output 2: Climate resilience is enhanced, and low carbon development strategies adopted.
Indicator 2.1: # of evidence-based assessments undertaken by sectors to inform climate change adaptation, mitigation, low-carbon transition, and inclusive green growth. Target: TBD Result: One assessment is underway. There is an assessment ongoing on systems-level level assessments in the cattle corridor that systems will generate climate-risk-informed evidence to catalyze transformative climate action at the sub-national level, and to guide the integration of the 2021 NDC and 2018 NAP-Ag into district-level development plans.
Indicator 2.2: # of men and women who use climate information services, and products Target: F-24.5 millions, M-23.8 millions Result: Climate information was received by 3000 farmers (55%) women, who were organized in 15 cooperatives that worked with CSAII project.
Indicator 2.3: Extent to which an integrated climate information and disaster early warning system is functional (SDG 1.5.3, SP 3.3.1) Indicator: Fully Result: Its fully functional
Indicator 2.4: % sectors, institutions, and local governments translating international and national climate change policies into concrete adaptation and mitigation plans and actions. Target: TBD Result: 1. MAAIF is implementing the NAP Ag (National Adaptation Plan for the Agriculture sector, through the FSURE project 2. MAAIF is also implementing the Climate Change Policy and Strategy through the National Climate Smart Programme (2021-2025). 3. MWE is translating the adaptation requirements of the Ramsar Convention into actions by implementing the Wetland Restoration Projects which are GCF, UNDP and ADA funded).
Indicator 2.5: # households applying sustainable and climate smart agricultural practices and value chains to improve crop and livestock productivity. Target: .TBD Result: 1) 5000 farmers (55% women) that worked with the CSAII project applied sustainable CSA practices to improve crop productivity. 2) 800 households organized in 20 Farmer Field Schools in the Districts of Nakapiripirit, Nabilatuk and Moroto applied CSA practices to improve pasture lands and livestock productivity.
Indicator 2.6: # cities supported to develop, finance, and implement climate change action plans. Target: TBD Result: Plans are underway to be achieved next year 2023 under SCALA project.
Indicator 2.7: # of documented climate change adaptation and mitigation best practices and lessons learned from the programme that influence/inform policy and practice. Target: TBD Result: 1. The practice of providing water for micro-irrigation was documented from the CSAII project and used to inform practice in the FSURE project, which is now establishing water harvesting for micro-irrigation. 2. The practice of storing cereals in plastic or metallic silos in the Eastern region of Uganda, significantly reduced post-harvest losses and has influenced practice in the FSURE project
